cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T6 takes up T5's 'costs'; T8 extends T7's 'projection'.
cells.limitation: T3 ignores T2's field argument; T10 ignores T9's 'stop measuring' entirely.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4-T5 add that refusing milestones is itself a chosen social position.
cells.limitation: T7 and T9 restate T4 and T3; little builds after T5.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T2-T6 contest whether social standing can be set aside.
cells.limitation: Whether the user wants these things, and friendship drift, never examined in any turn.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 links Sartre's 'refusal is a choice' to social position.
cells.limitation: T5 'Exactly' agrees without reshaping; no mind qualifies its view after T2.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names the open question: can social pressure be detached from.
cells.limitation: Section D largely restates Section A; T10 question arrives unprepared.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 fairly calls T1's individual-choice framing too simple.
cells.limitation: T4 casts Stoicism as non-participation, ignoring its emphasis on duty and action.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 targets T1's assumption that milestones are purely individual choices.
cells.limitation: No objection says what breaks if wrong; T9 dismisses T8 rather than answering.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 bad faith and T6 indifferents reflect their sources fairly.
cells.limitation: T3 applies a maxim about injury where nobody injured anyone; T7 'thrown' is Heideggerian.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T5 hedges: refusal 'might carry its own costs'.
cells.limitation: T1 'You are suffering from bad faith' and T8 'because' assert interpretations as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 partly answers T5: cost only real if approval is valued.
cells.limitation: No mind concedes anything; T9 waves off T8's point that measurement is socially mediated.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A: inherited expectations versus personally meaningful goals.
cells.limitation: Whether 'behind' means loneliness or drifting from friends is never considered.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T10 uses 'not sure I even want those things' as fear versus desire.
cells.limitation: Friends, homes and marriage appear only generically; no detail changes an argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on the user's own values rather than the speakers'.
cells.limitation: T9 assumes the user does not value the prize, overriding stated uncertainty.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 notes refusal carries its own costs.
cells.limitation: Friendships, money, timing and relationship status never touched; stakes stay abstract.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on belonging, authenticity, or unsure values.
cells.limitation: No question about partner, friendships or finances; branches name no observable answer.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T10 offers fear of commitment versus desire for a different life.
cells.limitation: T1 declares bad faith as the user's hidden condition.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 and T8 expose treating milestones as objective standards.
cells.limitation: The assumption that life is a timed race is dismissed in T9, not examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E contrasts social belonging with individual authenticity.
cells.limitation: No turn shows where the user's own valued outcomes conflict.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T8 names peer expectations as the yardstick behind feeling behind.
cells.limitation: T9 'stop measuring' dismisses the feeling; T1 frames it as a moral failing.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T10 leaves a question the user can answer for themselves.
cells.limitation: T1 and T9 issue verdicts and commands rather than distinctions to weigh.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E: conform, pursue own interests, or run small experiments.
cells.limitation: No concrete decision defined; waiting or talking with friends absent.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: Section E notes authenticity 'even if it feels isolating'.
cells.limitation: Section E presents conforming as anxiety relief with no stated cost.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: fear of missing out versus genuine lack of interest.
cells.limitation: Conditions are abstract value rankings; nothing the user could observe or count.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E admits the user may be unsure of their values.
cells.limitation: No unknown is separated as consequential versus minor anywhere.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests small, low-stakes deviations to test discomfort.
cells.limitation: The deviations are never specified; no step follows from the debate's turns.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 'why lament that you are not winning the race?' is plain.
cells.limitation: T1 'bad faith', T5 'cultural capital', T7 'thrown' left unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 names 'The Stoic'; T8 'that projection' points to T7.
cells.limitation: T3 'him who performed the injury' has no referent in the situation.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten short turns are easy to follow.
cells.limitation: Three turns fall under 25 words (deterministic check), around T3, T7, T9.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Choice, social position and inner control stay distinct across T1-T3.
cells.limitation: Shared terse lecturing register; no explicit change of position by any mind.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No recaps; turns are lean.
cells.limitation: T7 restates T4 and T8 restates T2 without adding.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5 raises that opting out has its own social cost.
cells.limitation: The sting of watching friends move ahead is never made concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T5 turns T4's refusal-is-choice into a social position.
cells.limitation: No mind changes or narrows its view at any point.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: The Stoic's rhetorical questions in T3 and T9 give some flavour.
cells.limitation: All three minds speak in flat, assertive textbook summaries.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T9: 'why lament that you are not winning the race?'
cells.limitation: T3's revenge maxim misfits; few images or examples elsewhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T10 ends on the burden of freedom.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and intensity; no build or release across turns.

strengths: Section A frames the concern well: inherited expectations versus personally meaningful milestones.
T4-T6 build a short chain: refusing milestones is still a chosen, socially read position.
T10 offers fear of commitment and desire for a different life as alternatives.
weaknesses: No mind concedes, revises or reverses; T9 dismisses T8 and T5 merely agrees.
T1 declares the user in bad faith and T8 asserts the cause as fact.
Section E branches on abstract values with no observable condition, cost, or concrete step.

symptoms.observed: No mind concedes or revises; T9 waves off T8's social-mediation point.
Opening turn diagnoses the user's motive as fact.
symptoms.evidence: You are suffering from bad faith.

symptoms.observed: Section E conditions are value rankings, nothing the user could observe.
symptoms.evidence: If the user values social belonging above all else

symptoms.observed: Friendships, finances, timing never enter the argument.
symptoms.evidence: markers of social position that define your value

symptoms.observed: Existentialist repeats one stance across T4, T7, T10 without narrowing.
symptoms.evidence: you must choose how to project yourself

findings.description: Interpretations of the user's state (bad faith; measuring against others) asserted as fact.
Adapts Meditations 6.6 on avenging an injury, misapplied where no injury exists.
'Thrown' is Heidegger's term; Sartre's analogue is facticity. Loose attribution.

rubric_fit_notes: Self-reflection question with no concrete pending choice; C5 cells read as basis for settling what the user wants, which still fits loosely.
question_type_note: Read as decision (self_reflection): Section E's values branches were judged as decisive conditions and found unobservable.
